text:
Ayla (design): quick design review: rethinking the version timeline action affordances. current hover-only rollback icon is invisible to keyboard users and confusing to new PMs. looking for alternatives.
Marco: Agreed. we should surface actions in three places: visible compact actions on hover for mouse, a kebab menu for keyboard/focus, and a persistent contextual panel for the selected version.
Tess: persistent panel sounds heavy. what about an inline flyout that opens when a version is focused (not on hover) and contains actions + a short reason preview? that keeps the timeline tidy.
Ayla (design): inline flyout on focus is promising. it would appear to the right of the dot and be dismissible via Esc. accessibility must ensure focus lands in the flyout first.
Ibrahim: implementation note: use aria-expanded on the version button and move focus into the flyout. on close return focus to the version button. also add aria-live updates when an action completes (e.g., "Rolled back to v12").
Marco: microcopy nit: the action label "Rollback" sounds scary. prefer "Revert traffic to this version" in the menu, and in the modal say "Re-route live traffic to this version" with a short note about audit logs.
Tess: +1. also add a small inline helper: "This will not delete historical data" to reduce anxiety.
Ayla (design): good. regarding confirmations: we should require an optional note for most rollbacks but make it required if traffic delta > 25%. also include a checkbox "I understand this will change live behavior" for >50% to be safe.
Ibrahim: for keyboard parity, the flyout menu should expose the same actions as the hover state and support arrow navigation. the kebab menu must be reachable via Tab and have accessible names.
Marco: perf: hovering timeline currently triggers detailed metrics fetch which makes hover feel janky. debounce 300ms and show a lightweight cached sparkline immediately, then fetch full metrics when the flyout opens.
Tess: visual: when a version is focused or hovered, add a dashed focus ring and expose a small action badge with a chevron. make sure contrast meets AA at 14px.
Ayla (design): CSS suggestion for the dashed ring and small badge: ```css .version-dot:focus { box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(2, 132, 199, 0.12); outline: none; } .action-badge { background: #f3f7ff; color: #08306b; border-radius: 4px; padding: 2px 6px; font-size: 12px; } ```
Ibrahim: also add keyboard-only visible label for the action badge using .sr-only so assistive tech reads it but it doesn't clutter visual UI.
Marco: undo UX: after applying a revert, show a toast with undo for 12s and an accessible description. if undo invoked, revert should be auditable. also log the admin + note for compliance.
Tess: copy for the toast: "Re-route applied to v12. Undo" and aria-live polite region with focusable undo link.
ci-bot: preview available for branch "ux/timeline-actions-flyout" at https://console.redwood.ai/preview/ux/timeline-actions-flyout :white_check_mark:
Ayla (design): I'll upload updated comps with the flyout + softened modal copy to Figma and include annotations for focus order.
Ibrahim: I'll implement aria attributes, focus transfer, and debounce logic. will also add unit tests for focus return and live-region announcements.
Marco: I'll update copy in the content repo and add the helper text strings and tooltip clarifications.
Tess: I'll run a quick a11y pass on the new frames once they're up; especially color contrast on small badges.
Ayla (design): thanks team. plan: land these changes next sprint. ping here if any accessibility blockers. :sparkles:
